name: El Dorado International Airport
before:
The second busiest airport in Latin America and by far the most important in Colombia, handling just under half of the country's air traffic. It sits mostly in the Fontibón district of Bogotá.

Its real strength is connections. El Dorado is the most connected airport in Latin America and twentieth most connected in the world as of 2024, with direct flights to North, Central and South America, the Caribbean, Europe and the Middle East. It is nicknamed the Hub of the Americas and is the main base for Avianca. For building a multi-country South America itinerary this is usually the cleanest routing point.

It is also Iberoamerica's most important cargo hub, with 760,000 tonnes passing through.

The quality is well regarded rather than merely adequate. Skytrax and the World Airport Awards have ranked it among the best in the world since 2016, best in South America, and 35th in the world's top 100 airports.

Two runways of 3,800 metres serve a 1,700 acre site. It is operated by OPAIN, a consortium including the company that runs Zurich Airport.
after:
El Dorado, in Bogotá, is Colombia's main airport and one of the busiest in Latin America.

Its real strength is connections. In OAG's 2024 ranking it was the most internationally connected airport in Latin America and 20th in the world. There are direct flights to Europe as well as across the Americas, and it is Avianca's main base.

For air cargo it leads Latin America.

Skytrax's 2026 awards, voted by travellers, named it the best airport in South America and 37th in the world.

It has two runways, each 3,800 metres long, and is run by OPAIN.

claims.claim: El Dorado is in Bogotá
claims.note: The location is kept at city level: the Fontibón district rests on Wikipedia alone (cut below). The coordinates put the airport 12.5 km north west of the city centre.

Straight-line distance from the city centre: 12.5 km (7.8 miles)
Bearing from the city centre: 325 degrees, which is north west

claims.claim: Colombia's main airport
claims.note: Aerocivil, the civil aviation authority, calls El Dorado 'the country's main airport' in its release of 10 December 2025. Reworded from 'by far the most important in Colombia'.

quote: Esta certificación confirma que El Dorado, el principal aeropuerto del país y uno de los más relevantes en América Latina

sources.quote: El Dorado is also by far the busiest and most important airport in Colombia

claims.claim: one of the busiest in Latin America
claims.inAfter: one of the busiest in Latin America
claims.note: Softened from 'the second busiest airport in Latin America' (cut below). Wikipedia says second after Guarulhos; a former head of Aerocivil told a Semana forum (21 May 2025) that El Dorado had been third in the region four years earlier and in 2024 passed Mexico City by 500,000 passengers; Aerocivil (10 December 2025) calls it one of the most important airports in Latin America. No 2025 regional ranking could be read: the operator's site (eldorado.aero) answers with a Radware CAPTCHA, and Aerocivil's traffic releases give national totals only.

sources.quote: It is the second busiest airport in Latin America, after São Paulo - Guarulhos International Airport

quote: hace cuatro años éramos el tercer aeropuerto de la región en cantidad de pasajeros. El año pasado superamos al aeropuerto Benito Juárez (Ciudad de México) por 500.000 pasajeros

sources.quote: uno de los más relevantes en América Latina

claims.claim: OAG's 2024 ranking: most internationally connected airport in Latin America and 20th in the world
claims.inAfter: In OAG's 2024 ranking it was the most internationally connected airport in Latin America and 20th in the world.
claims.note: Was 'the most connected airport in Latin America and twentieth most connected in the world as of 2024', unattributed. The ranking is OAG's Megahubs 2024 (international connectivity), which Wikipedia also cites, so it is named as OAG's and kept with its year. OAG's 2025 edition exists (page saved as oag-megahubs-2025) but its tables are a download behind a form, so the 2025 placing could not be read.

quote: Bogota (BOG) is the most connected airport in Latin America this year and is in 20th place globally

sources.quote: it is the most well-connected airport in Latin America, and is the 20th most connected in the world as of 2024

claims.claim: direct flights to Europe as well as across the Americas
claims.inAfter: There are direct flights to Europe as well as across the Americas
claims.note: Shortened from 'North, Central and South America, the Caribbean, Europe and the Middle East'; the Middle East is cut (below). Europe: the UK CAA counted 177,739 scheduled passengers between Heathrow and Bogotá in 2025. The Americas: OAG places Bogotá first for international connections among Latin American airports, and Wikipedia lists the regions.

sources.quote: El Dorado has direct international flights to North America, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, Europe, and the Middle East

quote: Rank Airport Country Dominant Carrier Share of Flights

claims.claim: Avianca's main base
claims.note: OAG (2024) names Avianca as the dominant airline at Bogotá with 56 per cent of flights. Avianca's own site, asked for its hubs page, served its fares page instead, which offers flights from Bogotá by default to eleven Colombian cities (read 23 September 2026).

sources.quote: It is the most important hub for the Colombian flag carrier Avianca

claims.claim: leads Latin America for air cargo
claims.inAfter: For air cargo it leads Latin America.
claims.note: Was 'Iberoamerica's most important cargo hub, with 760,000 tonnes passing through'. Aviacionline (23 September 2026) says El Dorado leads cargo traffic in Latin America, carried mainly by flower and coffee exports; the former Aerocivil head quoted by Semana (May 2025) put it a third ahead of Guarulhos, the second. The tonnage is cut (below).

quote: El Aeropuerto Internacional El Dorado de Bogotá lidera el tráfico de carga en América Latina

sources.quote: it is also Iberoamerica's most important cargo hub
En materia de carga, superamos por un tercio la cantidad de carga que lleva el segundo aeropuerto regional más relevante, que es Guarulhos (São Paulo)

claims.claim: Skytrax 2026: best airport in South America
claims.inAfter: Skytrax's 2026 awards, voted by travellers, named it the best airport in South America
claims.note: Was 'Skytrax and the World Airport Awards have ranked it ... best in South America', with no year. The World Airport Awards are Skytrax's own awards, not a second body. Skytrax's 2026 table of best airports in South America puts Bogotá first (Quito second, Lima fourth), and Aviacionline (22 September 2026) reports the title as current.

sources.quote: Best Airports in South America 2026 1 Bogota 2 Quito
voted by air travellers around the world in the 2025/2026 World Airport Survey

quote: El Dorado mantiene distinciones internacionales como la de Mejor Aeropuerto de Sudamérica por la auditora Skytrax

claims.claim: Skytrax 2026: 37th in the world
claims.inAfter: Skytrax's 2026 awards, voted by travellers, named it the best airport in South America and 37th in the world.
claims.note: Was '35th in the world's top 100 airports', Skytrax's 2023 placing (per Wikipedia). Skytrax's World's Top 100 Airports 2026 puts Bogotá 37th, up from 40th in 2025. The page was saved by the CTS helper and copied here with a NOTE line. Attributed to Skytrax, whose own table it is.

claims.claim: two runways of 3,800 metres
claims.inAfter: It has two runways, each 3,800 metres long

claims.claim: run by OPAIN
claims.note: Aviacionline (22 September 2026) calls Opain the concession holder at El Dorado; Aerocivil's release of 10 December 2025 speaks for OPAIN S.A. on the airport's operations.

quote: El plan de descarbonización de la concesionaria Opain en El Dorado
Por su parte, OPAIN S.A. destacó que este logro refuerza la solidez operativa del aeropuerto

claims.claim: second busiest airport in Latin America
claims.wasBefore: The second busiest airport in Latin America
claims.why: Softened to 'one of the busiest in Latin America' (above). The exact rank rests on Wikipedia and on 2024 figures quoted by a former Aerocivil head in May 2025; no 2025 ranking or 2025 passenger total for El Dorado could be read (operator's site behind a Radware CAPTCHA; Aerocivil's releases give national totals only).

claims.claim: by far the most important in Colombia
claims.wasBefore: by far the most important in Colombia
claims.why: Reworded to Aerocivil's own phrase, 'Colombia's main airport' (above).

claims.claim: handles just under half of the country's air traffic
claims.wasBefore: handling just under half of the country's air traffic
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (49 per cent, no year given). Aerocivil's releases give only national totals counted by origin and destination (57,520,767 passengers in 2025, each journey once), which cannot be set against an airport's own count, and its airport-level statistics page could not be found on its new site (the old address answers with Aerocivil's 404 page). The operator's site is behind a CAPTCHA.

claims.claim: sits mostly in the Fontibón district
claims.wasBefore: It sits mostly in the Fontibón district of Bogotá.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Fontibón local mayor's site (fontibon.gov.co) gave a remote connection failure, Bogotá's tourism site (bogotadc.travel) answered 403 and the operator's site is behind a CAPTCHA; none was tried again. The city is kept.

claims.claim: most connected in Latin America and twentieth in the world as of 2024 (unattributed)
claims.wasBefore: El Dorado is the most connected airport in Latin America and twentieth most connected in the world as of 2024
claims.why: Kept, but named as OAG's 2024 ranking (above), since OAG's 2025 placing could not be read.

claims.claim: direct flights to the Middle East (and the full list of regions)
claims.wasBefore: with direct flights to North, Central and South America, the Caribbean, Europe and the Middle East
claims.why: Shortened to Europe and the Americas (above). No second source for a current Middle East flight was found, and Wikipedia's own route notes put the Istanbul flight via Panama City and the Doha flight in the future ('will make a stop in Caracas').

quote: Turkish Airlines' flight from Bogotá to Istanbul makes a stop in Panama City.
Qatar Airways' flight from Bogotá to Doha will make a stop in Caracas.

claims.claim: nicknamed the Hub of the Americas
claims.wasBefore: It is nicknamed the Hub of the Americas
claims.why: Only Wikipedia calls it a nickname. Semana's May 2025 forum used the phrase as a question ('ready to be the hub of the Americas?'), a slogan rather than an established name.

claims.claim: the cleanest routing point for a multi-country South America itinerary
claims.wasBefore: For building a multi-country South America itinerary this is usually the cleanest routing point.
claims.why: An opinion no source makes. The OAG connectivity ranking it drew on is kept (above).

claims.claim: 760,000 tonnes of cargo
claims.wasBefore: Iberoamerica's most important cargo hub, with 760,000 tonnes passing through
claims.why: The tonnage has no year in Wikipedia's text and disagrees with Wikipedia's own infobox (809,021 tonnes in 2024) and with the former Aerocivil head quoted by Semana ('more than 810,000 tonnes a year'), so no figure is given. The ranking is kept as 'leads Latin America' (above), Aviacionline's wording.

claims.claim: quality well regarded rather than merely adequate
claims.wasBefore: The quality is well regarded rather than merely adequate.
claims.why: Framing; the Skytrax results themselves are kept (above).

claims.claim: ranked among the best since 2016, best in South America, 35th in the world
claims.wasBefore: Skytrax and the World Airport Awards have ranked it among the best in the world since 2016, best in South America, and 35th in the world's top 100 airports.
claims.why: Replaced by Skytrax's 2026 results (above): best in South America and 37th in the world. '35th' was the 2023 placing; 'since 2016' would need each year's table and is dropped; the World Airport Awards are Skytrax's own, not a second body.

claims.claim: a 1,700 acre site
claims.wasBefore: Two runways of 3,800 metres serve a 1,700 acre site.
claims.why: The site area rests on Wikipedia alone (the operator's site is behind a CAPTCHA). The runways are kept, reworded (above).

claims.claim: OPAIN is a consortium including the company that runs Zurich Airport
claims.wasBefore: It is operated by OPAIN, a consortium including the company that runs Zurich Airport.
claims.why: OPAIN is kept (above), but Flughafen Zürich's part could not be confirmed as current: flughafen-zuerich.ch answers with an Azure web application firewall page asking for JavaScript (a bot check, not tried again) and OPAIN's own site is behind a Radware CAPTCHA.

claims.claim: FCDO: only authorised taxis may pick up at El Dorado
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO says Bogotá's El Dorado only allows authorised taxis (yellow, white plates, numbers on doors and roof) to pick up passengers at its terminals, and warns of express kidnappings and robberies in unlicensed taxis. Useful to an agent, but nothing in the old text to replace. For Andy to decide.

quote: Bogotá’s El Dorado International Airport only allows authorised taxis to pick up passengers at its terminals.
There have been reports of express kidnappings, assaults and robberies in unlicensed taxis.

claims.claim: direct flights from London Heathrow
claims.why: Held back: the UK CAA counted 177,739 passengers between Heathrow and Bogotá in 2025 (177,540 in 2024), all on scheduled flights, the only UK route to Colombia in its table. The airline is not named by the table, and neither the operator's airline list (CAPTCHA) nor an airline page was read, so no carrier is given. The old text names no UK flight. For Andy to decide.

opinion.why: A signpost kept from the old text; it introduces OAG's connectivity ranking, which follows and is sourced.
